key_insight: Learning latent world models at multiple temporal scales enables coarse-to-fine hierarchical planning in latent space, reducing prediction error accumulation and drastically shrinking the search space for long-horizon control.
problem_solved: Addresses the difficulty of long-horizon model-based control where single-scale learned models accumulate prediction errors and face an exponentially large planning search space, limiting zero-shot generalization and practical deployment.
method: Train latent dynamics models at multiple temporal resolutions (e.g., fast short-horizon and slow long-horizon latent models) to capture both fine-grained control and abstract long-term structure.

Perform hierarchical planning: a high-level planner proposes coarse latent goals over long horizons using the slow model; a low-level MPC refines and executes short-horizon actions using the fast model.
Plan and optimize in latent space to reduce computational cost and mitigate prediction drift, enabling scalable, zero-shot-capable control in new environments.
impact: Makes long-horizon model-based control more reliable and scalable for embodied agents and robotics by combining abstraction with concrete short-term control—improving generalization and efficiency for practitioners building real-world planners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing two latent models (slow/long-horizon and fast/short-horizon) with arrows for high-level planning -> low-level MPC -> actions

paper_title: Hierarchical Planning with Latent World Models
paper_authors: Wancong Zhang, Basile Terver, Artem Zholus, Soham Chitnis, Harsh Sutaria
